tasks.title: Dreams of the Polar Bear
tasks.statement: Terrestrial Polar Bear-observer, watching the lunar disk in the phase of the full moon, in his dreams became thousand times closer to it. What did the magnitude of the Moon become? The solution has to include an artistic picture with an image of the Bear-observer on the North Pole.

parts.question: What did the magnitude of the Moon become?
parts.reference:
Solution: 7 pt in total, including:
Understanding about impossibility to use approximation of point-like objects - 3 pt.
Result approximately Ω0/Ω1 = 40 000 — 2 pt.
Formula and final calculations -12m.7 — 2m.5·log(40000) = -24m.2 — 2 pt.
Note: for any solution based on calculations in approximation of point-like objects or any answer resulting in larger than the Sun brightness total mark (except mark for the picture) should not be larger:
1 pt for group α,
0.5 pt for group β.
Artistic picture of the Bear — 1 pt.

tasks.title: Great oppositions
tasks.statement: Now great oppositions of Mars happen every 15 or 17 years. To simplify colonization of Mars, to improve environmental conditions on it, and to increase the effect of the great oppositions, our civilization has conceived an ambitious project: to reduce by 6.0% the semi-major axis of this planet’s orbit, while keeping the eccentricity of the orbit unchanged. How often will the great oppositions of Mars occur in the case of the new orbit?

parts.question: How often will the great oppositions of Mars occur in the case of the new orbit?
parts.reference:
Correct using Kepler’s III law and finding T1 = T0(A1/A0)^(3/2) = 1.713 years — 3 pt.
Correct finding synodic period ~2.4 years - 2 pt.
Understanding that the great opposition is one of five, and result 12 years - 3 pt.

tasks.title: Proxima Centauri
tasks.statement: Can the star Proxima Centauri be visible from the vicinity of Alpha Centauri by naked eye? («да-yes» or «нет-no»). Justify your solution by calculations of the corresponding apparent magnitude of Proxima Centauri.

parts.question: Can the star Proxima Centauri be visible from the vicinity of Alpha Centauri by naked eye? Justify your solution.
parts.reference:
Understanding to use formula d = (x^2 + y^2 + z^2)^(1/2) — 1 pt.
Correct formulae for x, y and z — 3x1 pt.
Correct final calculation of d — 1 pt.
Correct comparing with the magnitude as seen from the Earth and result of magnitude from αCen — 1.5 pt.
Final comparing with 6m and answer «да-yes» — 1.5 pt.

tasks.title: Hydroplanet
tasks.statement:
Hydroplanet consists of a rocky “core” of radius R and a thick layer of water surrounding it from all sides. Local humans live at the bottom of this world’s ocean (i.e., on the surface of the “core”), and hydrosphere is an analogue of our atmosphere for them. Local scientists observe astronomical objects from the bottom of the ocean. Like on our Earth, the duration of day-night period on Hydroplanet is T = 24 hours.
Points of your solution have to include drawings with all necessary sizes or angular sizes. The outer surface of the ocean is smooth, no waves or ripples.

parts.question: Find the minimum depth H of the ocean, for which celestial bodies will be visible at the horizon.
parts.reference:
Common part:
Understanding nature of effect, total reflection effect — 2 pt.
Correct drawing (also showing total reflection effect) — 1 pt.
Using refractive index of water n = 1.334, calculation of β, and R — 1.5 pt.
4.1. Answer: H = 0.334 R — 1.5 pt.

parts.question: What will be the duration of the day for inhabitants of the planet’s equator? The disk of the central star can be considered as a point source of light.
Calculate the value of “atmospheric” refraction at the horizon on such a planet.
parts.reference: Picture, calculation and correct answer — 1 pt.

tasks.title: Climate
tasks.statement: The XXXII (32nd) century AD. Due to unknown reasons, the Sun became cooler, not changing its size, and the inclination of ecliptic to the celestial equator plane decreased to zero. Scientists proved that the problem of preserving the Earth’s climate and the annual change of seasons can be solved by a small star, negligible mass, but similar to a main-sequence star, moving in a circular orbit around the Sun. The star will revolve around the Sun as an inner planet, resulting in establishing a temperature regime on the Earth similar to the actual one at Issyk-Kul: the average winter and summer temperatures are -3 and +17 degrees respectively.

parts.question: Estimate the temperature of the cool Sun.
parts.reference:
Understanding nature of the effect and conclusion synodic period is 1 year — 1 pt.
Calculation sidereal period = 0.5 years — 1 pt.
Radius of the orbit from the III Kepler's law — 1 pt.
Energy balances — 2 pt.
5.1. Temperature of the Sun — 1 pt.

parts.question: Estimate to what spectral class the star which will be placed in the desired orbit will correspond.
parts.reference: ΔM = -5/2m lg(0.0464) = 3m.3 and from the HR-diagram spectral type K3 — 2 pt.

tasks.title: Sombrero Galaxy
tasks.statement: The Sombrero Galaxy, M104, is known as a holder of one of supermassive black holes. Images of the galaxy and its center (left side) have angular sizes 10'×7' and 10.8"×7.2" respectively. To the right, three spectra from the Hubble space telescope (in the region containing the emission lines from ionized oxygen and nitrogen) are shown for regions around the center of the galaxy. The bottom spectrum is from a region around the very center, while other two spectra are from flanking region. The values on top of the dotted lines indicate the rest (laboratory) wavelength in Ångströms.

parts.question: Is M104 approaching us or receding from us? (Answer this question by sketch drawing.)
parts.reference: Spectra are redshifted, receding from us — 1 pt.

parts.question: Estimate the velocity of M104 towards us or away from us.
parts.reference:
z_avg = (Δλ/λ)_average = 0.0035 — 1 pt.
V = c z = 0.0036 x 300000 km/s = 1050 km/s — 1 pt.

parts.question: Roughly estimate the approximate mass of the supermassive black hole in the center of M104 (answer in solar masses m_⊙).
parts.reference:
L = V / H = 1050 km/s / 71 km/s/Mpc = 15 Mpc — 1 pt.
R(a.u.) = 0.54 x 15·10^6 = 8·10^6 — 1 pt.
Other correct calculations and obtaining the mass of the galactic center — 3 pt.
